reply:
You're absolutely right, and thank you for the correction. I had that backwards.

The number in parentheses — INT(11), INT(20), etc. — is purely a **display width hint** for formatting when ZEROFILL is used. It has no effect on the actual storage capacity of the data type.

INT is always a 32-bit signed integer, which ranges from -2,147,483,648 to 2,147,483,647 — roughly ±2.1 billion, capping out at 10 digits for positive values.

So to answer the original question correctly: **No, INT(11) cannot hold a 12-digit number**, not because of the "11" but because INT itself is limited to 10 digits. If you need to store 12-digit numbers, you'd need BIGINT, which is a 64-bit signed integer that can hold up to about 9.2 quintillion (19 digits).

Thanks for catching that!
